claim.pdf_says: Table 12 — Procedural statements (Continued), WRITE row. The 'Conditional phrase' cell prints TWO stacked lines: '[NOT] INVALID KEY' on the first line and '[NOT] END-OF-PAGE' on the second line. Explicit scope terminator: 'END-WRITE'.
claim.why_it_matters:
Same defect class as the DELETE row on page 563. '[NOT] INVALID KEY' and '[NOT] END-OF-PAGE' are mutually exclusive alternative conditional phrases of WRITE (INVALID KEY applies to relative/indexed files, END-OF-PAGE to LINAGE files); joined on one line they read as a single compound phrase. Sibling rows in the same table (IF, READ, SEARCH) correctly use '
'.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed at 300 dpi, and the refutation attempts all fail. (1) The PDF glyphs. Cropped and magnified the WRITE row of Table 12 on rendered page 565 (printed folio 535). The 'Conditional phrase' cell unambiguously prints two stacked lines: line 1 '[NOT] INVALID KEY', line 2 '[NOT] END-OF-PAGE'. The last row of the table is visibly double-height to accommodate them. The markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23625, and the page-565 work-unit slice line 14) prints them on one line separated by a single space, with no separator glyph at all. (2) The strongest refutation — 'it is just incidental word-wrap inside a narrow cell, i.e. formatting' — is disproved by measurement, not by eyeballing. Vertical rules of the table sit at x=1012 and x=1607, so the Conditional-phrase cell is 595 px wide; text is inset 25 px (first glyph at x=1037), giving roughly 545-570 px of usable line width. Word segmentation of the two printed lines gives '[NOT]'=106 px, 'INVALID'=161 px, 'KEY'=75 px, 'END-OF-PAGE'=268 px, inter-word space ~17 px. A greedy wrap of the single string '[NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT] END-OF-PAGE' would therefore set '[NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT]' on line 1 (500 px used, ending at x=1537, comfortably inside the ~1557-1582 px right limit) and 'END-OF-PAGE' alone on line 2. That is NOT what the page prints. The observed line 1 stops after 'KEY' at x=1414, ~125 px short of the wrap point, and line 2 begins with '[NOT]'. A break placed short of the available measure is a hard break, not a wrap. So the PDF encodes two separate entries, exactly at the phrase boundary. (3) The transcription's own convention corroborates it. Within this same Table 12, ISO_COBOL.md line 23582 has '| IF | THEN
ELSE | END-IF |', line 23593 '| READ | [NOT] AT END
[NOT] INVALID KEY | END-READ |', line 23600 '| SEARCH | WHEN
AT END | END-SEARCH |'. The READ row is structurally identical to WRITE (two bracketed alternative phrases stacked) and preserved the break as '
'; WRITE (23625) and DELETE (23561, '[NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT] ON EXCEPTION') did not. So the flattening is an inconsistency internal to the transcription, not a faithful rendering of a differently-typeset cell. (4) Neither source is misquoted: the claim's PDF quote and markdown quote both match byte-for-byte what I read. (5) It is not page-break furniture, not hyphenation, and the loss does change how the cell reads: the cell is a list of the conditional phrases a statement may take, and dropping the only delimiter between two list items lets '[NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT] END-OF-PAGE' parse as one compound phrase. The two are in fact mutually exclusive for WRITE (INVALID KEY for relative/indexed, END-OF-PAGE for sequential files with LINAGE), so the flattened reading is not merely ambiguous, it is wrong. No normative rule text is lost, so 'cosmetic' severity stands. The claim is accurate as written; the fix is '[NOT] INVALID KEY
[NOT] END-OF-PAGE'.
verdict.corrected_description:
Accurate as filed; one detail worth recording for the fix. Page 565 (printed folio 535), Table 12 — Procedural statements (Continued), WRITE row: the PDF prints the Conditional-phrase cell as two hard-broken lines, '[NOT] INVALID KEY' over '[NOT] END-OF-PAGE', with 'END-WRITE' as the explicit scope terminator. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23625 flattens them to '| WRITE | [NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT] END-OF-PAGE | END-WRITE |', losing the item separator. The break is demonstrably semantic rather than word-wrap: the cell affords ~545-570 px of line width and '[NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT]' occupies only ~500 px, so a wrapping engine would have pulled the second '[NOT]' up to line 1; the PDF instead breaks ~125 px early, at the phrase boundary. Fix: '| WRITE | [NOT] INVALID KEY
[NOT] END-OF-PAGE | END-WRITE |', matching the '
' convention already used by the IF (23582), READ (23593) and SEARCH (23600) rows of the same table. The DELETE row (23561) carries the identical defect and should be swept in the same change.
